Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Traffic heatmap & lead-gen scenarios — Moscone West Q4

Hi all,

I sketched a first-pass visitor heatmap for our Moscone West island (attached: visitor_heatmap_v1.png) and a simple lead-flow matrix (leadflow_matrix_v2.xlsx). Goal is to decide: 1) primary demo lane vs. lounge/meeting pockets, 2) where to place the lead capture stations, and 3) how signage should drive traffic.

Key asks:
- Alice: can BrightEvents mock up 2 alternate booth flows (A = demo-forward, B = lounge-forward) and call out staffing needs?
- Marissa/Tessa: which flow better supports our SDR+AE handoff? are we prioritizing high-volume demos or longer meetings?
- Grace: any compliance/access constraints we should bake in for crates/AV?

Attachments: visitor_heatmap_v1.png, leadflow_matrix_v2.xlsx

Planning note: we have a site walk week of 11/02 — would like vendor mockups before then.

Thanks,
Marcus
Sr. Field Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-25 11:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Traffic heatmap & lead-gen scenarios — Moscone West Q4

Marcus — thanks for the packet. We can put together two flow options and a short crew estimate by Friday (10/29). Quick clarifying q's:
1) Is the demo footprint 10x20 or 20x20? the heatmap seems closer to a 20x20 island.
2) How many concurrent demo stations are we aiming for (2 / 4 / 6)?

Initial thoughts: if you want high lead velocity, route people past an interactive demo first and capture leads before the lounge. If you want deeper conversations with prioritized accounts, build a pull-through lounge that encourages booking. We can annotate where charging stations/digital forms should go to minimize queueing.

I'll include a simple queue-time calc for each scenario.

—Alice
Senior Events Producer
BrightEvents

Attachment: (will include mockups PDF in next email)

--- Message 3/6 ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-26 08:45 PDT
Subject: Re: Traffic heatmap & lead-gen scenarios — Moscone West Q4

Quick responses:
- Footprint: confirmed 20x20 island (per venue booking).
- Concurrent demo stations: target 4 active demos during peak hours; 2 for product walk-thrus and 2 for quick trial/walk-up.
- Lead capture: A hybrid model — one fixed tablet kiosk at the front for badge-scan capture + 2 roaming tablets for AEs. We still want a staffed lead desk to triage P1 accounts.

Operational asks for Alice: please annotate where crate opening/AV power drops are required and leave a 4ft clear egress corridor on the east side (venue rule).

I'll update the leadflow_matrix with priority account tags and expected talk-time (attached v2).

Thanks — Marissa
Director, Field Marketing
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: leadflow_matrix_v2.xlsx

Couple of tactical notes:
- Staffing: plan for 2 AEs per demo rotation (4 AEs total peak), plus 2 SDRs at lead desk. Shift planning will be in 3.5–4 hour blocks.
- Swag & give-away placement: put quick-swag near the demo exit to reinforce capture.
- Charging spots: need 2 power islands for tablets; vendor needs cable covers for safety.

I'll run an initial rota and share by Friday.

—Tessa
Events Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Team — quick venue constraints to note after reviewing your sketch:
- The east-side 4ft corridor Marissa mentions must remain clear at all times for emergency egress; no temporary displays in that zone.
- Power: available floor drops in grid A2 and B3 only; any additional drops require order with Exhibitor Services (lead time 10 business days).
- Rigging: overhead banners allowed up to 12ft; any structural loads must be approved and insured.

Also attaching the exhibitor floor_restrictions.pdf that lists forbidden materials and forklift windows. For crate deliveries, use Gate 4 between 06:00–10:00 on move-in day; Gate 2 is reserved for other shows.

—Carlos
Exhibitor Services
Moscone Center

Attachment: floor_restrictions.pdf
